narrative:
The bank’s decision to deny your loan was based on an analysis of your financial profile, which suggested a higher likelihood of difficulty repaying the loan compared to other applicants. The model estimated that you had a **44% chance of being a bad credit risk**—meaning there was nearly a one-in-two possibility that repaying the loan could become challenging. Since the bank uses a threshold of **25% or higher** to make this call, your application was unfortunately declined.

The decision wasn’t made randomly—it was influenced most strongly by three key factors in your financial situation. The most significant was your **lack of documented savings**. Unlike many approved applicants who had some savings, even small amounts, your financial records didn’t show any. This made the bank concerned about your ability to cover unexpected expenses or absorb financial setbacks without relying on the loan itself.

Another important factor was your **credit history**, which showed that while you’ve paid back past loans successfully, the model still flagged this as a moderate risk signal compared to applicants with an even stronger track record of on-time payments. Finally, the fact that you already have **other payment plans through a bank**—something rare among approved applicants—suggested to the model that you might be stretched thin financially, even if your current loan payments are manageable.

While your **long-term job stability** (having worked in your role for 4-7 years) and **homeownership** worked in your favor, these positive signs weren’t enough to outweigh the concerns about your savings and existing financial commitments. To improve your chances next time, focus on **building savings**—even modest amounts can reassure lenders—and consider paying down or consolidating any existing debts to show stronger financial flexibility. If possible, avoiding new payment obligations before applying could also help.

The dataset contains information on a series of debtors that took a loan from the bank.

The target variable is whether the applicant will be a bad credit risk.

Protected attributes sex, age and foreign_worker were not used to make the machine prediction.
